intent.title: Switch between Desktop, Laptop, Tablet and Phone breakpoints
steps: Click Laptop, Tablet, Phone and Desktop in the top bar.
expected: The page width inside the iframe becomes 1180 CSS px for Laptop, 834 for Tablet, 390 for Phone and 1440 for Desktop; in Fit mode the canvas refits the zoom.
The status bar shows the active breakpoint; the buttons show their widths in tooltips.
The breakpoint buttons and the canvas widths read one breakpoint table (a unit test checks it).
The active breakpoint is restored after a reload.

intent.title: Style overrides per breakpoint, desktop first
steps: Select a Heading at Desktop with font size 32px.
Switch to Tablet and set font size 24px; switch to Phone and look at it.
expected: The Tablet value is stored as an override for tablet in the document JSON; at Tablet and Phone the computed font size is 24px, at Desktop and Laptop 32px.
Fields with an override at the active breakpoint show a badge naming the breakpoint; inherited values show where they come from.
Resetting the override returns Tablet and Phone to 32px.
styles.css contains the base rule and @media (max-width: 834px) with the override, in cascade order.
The export media queries read the same breakpoint table as the buttons and the canvas (unit test).

intent.title: Style states: hover, focus, active, disabled, invalid and placeholder shown
steps: Select a Button, choose State Hover and set background colour and opacity.
Choose Focus and set an outline; choose Base.
Switch to Tablet and set a Hover value there.
expected: The State menu lists Base, Hover, Focus, Active, Disabled, Invalid and Placeholder shown; while a state is chosen a canvas badge reads 'Editing Hover' [canvas.badge.editingState] and the canvas shows the element with that state's values.
State values are stored per state (and per breakpoint) in the document JSON and do not change the base values.
styles.css contains :hover, :focus and @media rules for them; in the exported page hovering the button changes its computed background.
